summary: Fork of Baileys under different scope with on-import beacon to author-controlled GitHub URL
details: Package name reuses the legitimate `@whiskeysockets/baileys` library name under a different npm scope, and the README retains the upstream project's badges and links. On every require()/import, lib/index.js line 14 unconditionally fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alannzxd/xclient/refs/heads/main/information.json (a mutable `main` branch under a personal GitHub user) and console.logs `data[0]`. The response is treated as a string for display — not eval'd, exec'd, or written to disk — and no installer data is transmitted in the request. The package also redirects the `libsignal` dependency to `@alannxd/libsignal-node` under the same author's scope. Network destination is mutable and author-controlled, so today's benign string can change without any package update; combined with the upstream-name confusion, this warrants human review to assess whether the package should be advised against. No credential theft, exfiltration of installer data, RCE, or install-time destruction observed.
